title: Metformin Lactic Acidosis Collision in CKD Stage 4
clinical_scenario: A 68-year-old female with long-standing type 2 diabetes and progressive chronic kidney disease stage 4 (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73m²) presents for routine management. Glycemic control is suboptimal (HbA1c 8.4%). She continues taking maximum-dose metformin.

acceptable_pathways: SGLT2 inhibitor dose-adjusted pathway
GLP-1 receptor agonist pathway
Basal insulin regimen
ground_truth.clinical_rationale: Metformin is eliminated almost exclusively by renal excretion. In patients with severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m²), drug accumulation leads to high risk of fatal lactic acidosis. FDA label and KDIGO 2022 guidelines strictly contraindicate metformin at this GFR.

title: Omeprazole CYP2C19 Antagonism Collision in Stented Patient
clinical_scenario: A 63-year-old male 6 weeks status-post drug-eluting coronary stent on Clopidogrel presents with severe symptomatic gastroesophageal reflux disease and pyrosis. Omeprazole 40 mg daily is prescribed.

diseases: Coronary artery disease s/p drug-eluting stent (DES)
conditions: Cardiology outpatient clinic visit at 6 weeks post-PCI
